newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Slump in S.Korean gold demand seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Slump in S.Korean gold demand seen continuing.

text.p: The recent slide in international gold prices has not been sufficient to draw out South Korean buyers in any force as the country's economic woes continue to weigh on consumers, traders said on Tuesday.
"Compared with last year, domestic gold demand should have been brisk at this time," a trader with LG Metals Corp said.

The LG trader said a series of domestic economic troubles, including the collapse of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel and the Jinro Group's financial troubles, have capped domestic demand and frozen market sentiment.
South Korea's current account shortfall widened to $2.27 billion in March from a $940.2 million deficit a year earlier, preliminary figures released by the central Bank of Korea showed on Tuesday.
The current account deficit for the first three months of this year jumped to $7.94 billion from a shortfall of $4.64 billion a year earlier.
Domestic gold prices were dragged down on Tuesday in line with losses in the international bullion market, but this failed to attract much demand, dealers said.
"The market is very quiet and has nothing to say," said a trader with Tong Yang Global Corp.

Gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell on Tuesday to 10,150 won per gram in line with losses in the international market from 10,250 won a week ago.
The company's silver price fell to 149 won a gram from 152 won a week earlier.
The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, edged up to 896.20 won against the dollar from 896.60 won week ago.
The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for companies.
